solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Drink and hot dog after spending penny (5)

indicators.note: money you have spent is no longer with you, so once the penny is spent the dog has lost it

blocks.note: H = hot, as on a tap

annotation.surface: Someone nips to the loo, then comes back to a drink and a hot dog.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spending a penny' is British slang for going to the toilet, which is the picture the surface leans on; in the wordplay it is literal.
annotation.definitionFit: Hooch is slang for cheap or illicitly made liquor, so a drink by example.

entries.clue: Falcon is extremely tedious for keen birdwatchers, perhaps (9)

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters are wanted

blocks.note: the hobby is a small falcon
first and last letters of TEDIOUS

annotation.surface: A birdwatcher's grumble that falcons are dull.
annotation.walkthrough: The falcon fits the birdwatching surface perfectly, which hides that the bird's name is also a word for a pastime. 'Perhaps' flags birdwatchers as only one kind of enthusiast.
annotation.definitionFit: Keen birdwatchers pursue a pastime, so they are one example of the answer.

entries.clue: Concerning prisoner in prison camp (5)

blocks.note: of = concerning, as in 'tales of the sea'
an old lag is a long-serving convict

annotation.surface: A report about a prisoner held in a camp.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container instruction but only joins the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An Oflag was a German prisoner-of-war camp for officers, such as Colditz.

entries.clue: Investigation about Duke’s representation of manhood (8)

indicators.note: about means around, so the investigation goes around the duke

blocks.note: a hearing is an official inquiry

annotation.surface: An inquiry into how a duke is portrayed as a man.
annotation.walkthrough: HEA-D-RING: the duke sits inside the hearing. The answer is obscure: a ring worn in the hair by Zulu men once they reached full adult status.
annotation.definitionFit: The Zulu headring was worn by married men as a badge of maturity, so it stood for manhood.

entries.clue: Right after litigation, women damaged garden equipment (9)

indicators.note: right comes after litigation in the finished word, trailing it as part of the jumble
something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters of WOMEN plus R lose their order

blocks.note: used as printed, then rearranged with R

annotation.surface: A legal dispute, and then some women wreck the garden kit.
annotation.walkthrough: Only the women and the R are jumbled; the litigation stays intact at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain example: the machine that cuts the lawn is standard garden equipment.

entries.clue: Dead on time? No (4)

blocks.note: used of someone recently dead, before their name

annotation.surface: A curt verdict on whether something died punctually.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition is a little question and answer: asked if it was on time, the reply is no.
annotation.definitionFit: Used before a name, the word means recently dead; in everyday use it means not on time.

entries.clue: Publication supporting club is source of disagreement (5,5)

indicators.note: in a down clue a support holds from beneath, so the publication goes below the club

blocks.note: a wedge is a golf club

annotation.surface: A club newsletter that causes rows among members.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Club' reads as a society with a newsletter; it is the golf club.
annotation.definitionFit: A political term for a divisive topic used to split opponents' supporters, so a source of disagreement.

entries.clue: Procedure of drug overdose (6)

annotation.surface: A grim account of how a drug overdose happens.
annotation.walkthrough: The medical surface makes 'procedure' look like a hospital treatment; it is simply a way of doing things.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a set way of doing something.

entries.clue: Very parsimonious treasurer initially with good intentions (4-5)

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the treasurer's opening letter is used

annotation.surface: A stingy club treasurer who at least has his heart in the right place.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a character sketch of a tight-fisted treasurer, so 'very' looks like a mere intensifier rather than a word to be replaced.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective for an act done with good intentions even if it misfires.

entries.clue: Fanatical Scotsman regularly wild (5)

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every second letter of wild is taken

blocks.note: Rab, a Scots form of Robert, stands for any Scotsman
second and fourth letters of wIlD

annotation.surface: A fervent, untamed Scotsman.
annotation.walkthrough: Crosswords use common Scottish first names such as Ian, Mac and Rab to stand for a Scotsman.
annotation.definitionFit: Figuratively, the rage of a mad dog applied to views held with fanatical zeal.

entries.clue: Made steady jockey stable lad (9)

indicators.note: as a verb, to jockey is to jostle and manoeuvre for position, so the letters shift about

annotation.surface: A jockey and a stable lad calming a horse at the yard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jockey' is a noun in the racing picture, but it works as the verb, jostle. 'Steady' and 'stable' both sit in the surface to misdirect.
annotation.definitionFit: Ballast is weight added low in a ship to keep it steady, so adding it made the ship steady.

entries.clue: Fundamentalist thanks liberal (5)

annotation.surface: A hardliner thanks a liberal, an unlikely exchange.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sets a fundamentalist against a liberal as opposites, yet the liberal supplies half the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The singular of Taliban, the Islamic fundamentalist movement in Afghanistan.

entries.clue: In tent, turn back what culture may have produced (6)

indicators.note: the reversed turn is placed inside the tent
going back means the word runs from its end to its start

blocks.note: a yurt is a round felt tent of the Central Asian steppe
a go = a turn, as in 'your go'

annotation.surface: A camper inside a tent wondering what civilisation has produced.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Culture' reads as civilisation or the arts; here it is a bacterial culture, which is what thickens milk.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint by example: live bacterial cultures added to milk produce it.

entries.clue: Warped behaviour breaks contract (8)

indicators.note: to break into something is to split it open, so behaviour splits the contract

blocks.note: a deed is a legal contract

annotation.surface: Twisted conduct leads someone to break an agreement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Breaks contract' reads as a single phrase for reneging; 'breaks' is the insertion.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: bent or twisted out of its proper shape.

entries.clue: Break into building and suffer injury stealing clubs (5,1,4)

indicators.note: what is stolen is taken in and held, so the injury takes the clubs inside

annotation.surface: A burglar breaks in, gets hurt, and makes off with some golf clubs.
annotation.walkthrough: The C slips in just before RIB. The phrase is old thieves' cant, in which a crib was a house.
annotation.definitionFit: Old criminal slang for burgling a house, crib being cant for a dwelling.

entries.clue: No promises broken in garbled statement (10)

indicators.note: the promises are broken in the surface, and broken letters come apart and reassemble

annotation.surface: Someone backs out of promises in a muddled statement.
annotation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the definition describes the kind of wordplay that swaps sounds, such as 'a blushing crow' for 'a crushing blow'.
annotation.definitionFit: A slip that swaps the initial sounds of words, named after Rev. William Spooner, so a garbled statement.

entries.clue: Subtle meanings in obvious jokes (9)

blocks.note: as in 'have you heard the one about...'

annotation.surface: Subtle meanings buried in crude jokes.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sets subtle against obvious; the less familiar step is a joke being called a 'one'.
annotation.definitionFit: Figuratively, the extra harmonics above a note: implied meanings beyond the literal.

entries.clue: Rear is fine part of the body (4)

blocks.note: an arm is a body part

annotation.surface: Someone admiring a shapely backside as their best feature.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rear' looks like a noun, a bottom, and the body-part surface keeps it that way; it is the verb, to raise animals.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to farm livestock is to rear it.

entries.clue: Irrational individual had misinterpreted boring question (3,6)

indicators.note: a word misinterpreted is read wrongly, so its letters come out in a different order
boring means drilling into, so the jumbled letters go inside the question

blocks.note: a matter = a question, as in 'a matter of taste'
HAD rearranged, going in after the first letter

annotation.surface: Someone got a dull question wrong and seemed irrational.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like dull; it means drilling into. The character is from Alice in Wonderland, where he is simply 'the Hatter'.
annotation.definitionFit: By example: the Hatter at the tea party is the byword for irrational behaviour.

entries.clue: Incapacitated, carried out clutching fur (8)

indicators.note: to clutch is to hold tightly, so one word holds the other inside it

blocks.note: did = carried out, as in 'did the job'

annotation.surface: An injured person being carried out, still clutching a fur coat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Carried out' pictures a stretcher; it is simply a past tense of 'do'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: put out of action.

entries.clue: Stop baseball team returning (4)

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the team's name runs backwards

annotation.surface: A plea to halt a baseball team's comeback.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Returning' reads as the team coming home, not as a direction to read the name backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to stem a flow of blood or water is to stop it.

entries.clue: Well-versed expert hosts charming Democrat (10)

indicators.note: a host has guests inside his house, so the expert takes the other word inside

annotation.surface: A knowledgeable pundit entertaining a charming Democrat.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the Democrat is the guest, but it only tags on at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: Acquainted with a subject means familiar with it, so well-versed.

entries.clue: Go pale, affected in crowded city (6)

indicators.note: the first piece is placed in the second

blocks.note: hit = affected, as in 'hit by the news'
a wen is a cyst; William Cobbett called London 'the Great Wen'

annotation.surface: Someone blanches, overwhelmed by a crowded city.
annotation.walkthrough: Crosswords use wen for any overgrown, crowded city, after Cobbett's nickname for London.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to become white or pale.

entries.clue: Wife with better method of contraception (5,3)

blocks.note: 'my old Dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife

annotation.surface: A wife with a more reliable form of birth control.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as an adjective; it is the verb, to outdo.
annotation.definitionFit: British name for a contraceptive diaphragm.

entries.clue: Entrance to building opened by new benefactor (5)

indicators.note: a door opened by something has it standing in the gap, so the letter sits inside

annotation.surface: A building's entrance ceremonially opened by its generous patron.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a patron cutting the ribbon; 'opened by' is the insertion.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: one who gives money or goods.

entries.clue: Possibly ram Greek character (6)

blocks.note: the surface offers a sheep; read it as a young sheep's da (dad), since a ram may be a father
the surface suggests a person from Greece; it is a letter of the Greek alphabet

annotation.surface: A guess that a Greek figure might be a ram.
annotation.walkthrough: Split the answer as LAMB DA: a lamb's da, its dad, could be a ram. 'Possibly' allows that not every ram is a father.
annotation.definitionFit: Lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet.

entries.clue: What might be seen in jackboOTs? (5)

definitions.text: What might be seen in jackboOTs?

blocks.note: two letters are printed in capitals, so they are large

annotation.surface: A question about who wears jackboots.
annotation.walkthrough: The printed capitals are the wordplay: jackboOTs shows a big OT. Read whole, jackboots evoke fascist thugs, and an intolerant person might be found in them.
annotation.definitionFit: Jackboots symbolise authoritarian bullying, so an intolerant person is who might be seen wearing them.

entries.clue: Beware large hole in the ground (4)

blocks.note: a hollow in rock or earth

annotation.surface: A warning shouted at the edge of a pit.
annotation.walkthrough: The Latin word was British public-school slang, shouted by a lookout when a master approached.
annotation.definitionFit: Schoolboy slang for 'look out', and in ordinary English a large natural hollow underground.

entries.clue: Piece of music at last in 4/4 time (5)

indicators.note: at last means at the very end, so only the final letter of 'in' is used

annotation.surface: A musician's note about a piece written in common time.
annotation.walkthrough: 4/4 reads as a time signature in the musical surface; it is simply a fraction equal to one.
annotation.definitionFit: By example: a composition for nine performers is one kind of piece of music.

entries.clue: Nobleman punches to avenge shiner (4,5)

indicators.note: a punch drives into its target, so the nobleman goes into the other word

blocks.note: to right a wrong is to avenge it

annotation.surface: A nobleman throws punches to repay a black eye.
annotation.walkthrough: A shiner is slang for a black eye, which the fighting surface supports; here it means literally something that shines.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: the lamp at the back of a vehicle is something that shines.

entries.clue: Part of heel-bone sore when twisted a bit (4,5)

indicators.note: the letters wanted are only part of the words that follow
twisted round, so the hidden letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: the run from the second E of heel to the R of sore

annotation.surface: Complaint of a heel that is sore after being twisted a little.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A bit' reads as 'slightly'; it is a coin, as in a threepenny bit. The anatomy surface makes 'part of' look like a bone.
annotation.definitionFit: Bit as in threepenny bit means a coin, and this was a medieval English gold coin.

entries.clue: Inhibit weightwatcher? Not I (5)

indicators.note: 'Not I' says the I is absent, so it is taken out

annotation.surface: A dieter insisting 'Not me' when urged to show restraint.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags weightwatcher as a definition by example: any dieter will do.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to discourage someone from acting.
